note: Each suggestion is a decision for the owner, not a change already made. None of them has been implemented. The reviewer picks a disposition; a suggestion marked 'Declined' stays on the page with the reason so the decision is auditable.

suggestions.title: Publish a decision register before publishing any strategy
suggestions.problem: The site had strategy tables and validation gates but no single place listing which questions must be answered, by whom, and what evidence would answer them. Readers had to reconstruct the blockers from prose.
suggestions.proposal: Keep a register of every open question with its current answer, the evidence held, the evidence missing and an owner. Publish it as its own page and link it from every strategy row.
suggestions.rationale: A decision that cannot be traced to its open questions gets made on vibes. The register also makes it visible when the honest answer is 'we do not know'.
suggestions.evidence: This repository's own review: the 22 open review flags were spread across eight pages with no single entry point.
suggestions.effort: Medium — a data file plus one generated page; no new dependency.
suggestions.risk: The register decays into a museum if it is not regenerated by the build. Mitigation: it is generated, tested, and a stale file fails CI.
suggestions.gate: Must exist before any strategy is ranked (supports G01, G08).

suggestions.title: Keep a reviewable suggestions board instead of implementing improvements directly
suggestions.problem: Improvement ideas were being applied as they occurred, so there was no record of what was considered and rejected, and no way to compare two options before choosing.
suggestions.proposal: One page, one row per suggestion, with problem, proposal, rationale, effort, risk, the gate it serves, a source link and a disposition the owner sets. Nothing on the page is auto-applied.
suggestions.rationale: It gives the owner a choice between paths before any change lands, which is exactly what was asked for, and it leaves an audit trail of declined ideas.
suggestions.evidence: Requested directly by the owner in the 2026-11-12 brief.
suggestions.effort: Low — data file plus one generated page.
suggestions.risk: Suggestions can pile up faster than they are decided. Mitigation: every row shows a disposition, so an undecided backlog is visible rather than hidden.
suggestions.gate: Supports G08 (declared trial count) by recording what was tried.

suggestions.title: Archive the injury report with timestamps instead of one page state
suggestions.problem: The official injury page shows only the current state of the week's report. Without an archive, no one can tell what was knowable at a given kickoff, so no availability strategy can ever pass the temporal gate.
suggestions.proposal: Capture each day's report as a dated snapshot with the capture time recorded, and store it separately from the rendered page. One file per capture, hashed.
suggestions.rationale: This is the single highest-value data addition available from an official source, and it is the blocker named in gate G02 for every availability strategy.
suggestions.evidence: The Week 10 page read on 2026-11-12 has no per-report timestamp in its content, and four clubs on bye are simply absent, which makes a 'no news' club indistinguishable from a club not yet reported.
suggestions.effort: Medium — a capture script plus a dated file convention.
suggestions.risk: NFL.com Terms §1.3 restricts systematic retrieval and compilation. Any automated capture must be reviewed against those terms before it runs, which is why this is a proposal and not a build.
suggestions.gate: Unblocks G02 and G03 for division D-D.

suggestions.title: Record which clubs publish a usable depth chart, and never infer one
suggestions.problem: NFL.com club pages under /teams/<club>/depth-chart return a 404 for at least one club tested, while the club's own domain serves a chart. Coverage is therefore uneven and cannot be assumed.
suggestions.proposal: Keep a per-club coverage table: chart present or absent, the exact URL that worked, and the number of strings listed. Absent clubs stay blank rather than being filled from another source.
suggestions.rationale: The availability analysis is only as good as its coverage, and a reader must be able to see which clubs are simply not covered.
suggestions.evidence: https://www.nfl.com/teams/washington-commanders/depth-chart returned the site's 404 page on 2026-11-12; https://www.commanders.com/team/depth-chart served a full chart. Three club charts are transcribed here, 29 are not.
suggestions.effort: Low for the table, medium to expand coverage club by club.
suggestions.risk: Club depth charts are unofficial coaching estimates and change without notice, so the archive date matters as much as the content.
suggestions.gate: Raises coverage for G03; does not by itself satisfy it.

suggestions.title: Separate 'listed on the report' from 'will not play' in every availability display
suggestions.problem: A player appearing on the injury report is not the same as a player missing the game. Mixing the two inflates the apparent injury pressure on a club.
suggestions.proposal: Show four distinct columns: listed, did not practise, carries a game status, and Out. Never collapse them into one 'injuries' number.
suggestions.rationale: It is the difference between a signal and noise. A club with eleven listed players and zero Out designations is not depleted.
suggestions.evidence: Week 10: 26 clubs listed a total of 276 player rows, but only a small minority carried any game status at all. Two clubs rendered 'No Injuries Reported' and four were on bye.
suggestions.effort: Low — column design in the generator.
suggestions.risk: More columns are harder to scan. Mitigation: default sort by game status, with the raw counts available.
suggestions.gate: Improves G02 interpretation; prevents a false availability signal.

suggestions.title: Treat an unreproducible published average as missing, not as data
suggestions.problem: Four of 32 rows in the official team passing table show a per-attempt average that cannot be reproduced from that same table's attempts and yards.
suggestions.proposal: Compute every derived rate from the integers and publish the computed value labelled as derived. Where the page's own figure disagrees, exclude the page figure and record the discrepancy as a review item.
suggestions.rationale: A rate whose definition cannot be confirmed is not verifiable, and publishing it invites a reader to treat a rounding artefact as a statistic.
suggestions.evidence: KC 2037 yards / 263 attempts = 7.745, page shows 7.8; JAX 8.546 shown as 8.6; SEA 7.253 shown as 7.2; PIT 6.452 shown as 6.4. The rounding direction is inconsistent, so the definition of the column is unknown.
suggestions.risk: Derived rates will differ in the last decimal from the published ones, which needs a visible note to avoid looking like an error.

suggestions.title: Never publish a division rank that needs a tie-breaker
suggestions.problem: Division standing is not the same as win-loss order. Head-to-head, division record, common games and strength of victory are applied before points differential.
suggestions.proposal: Show a plain record rank from win percentage, explicitly labelled as a record rank, and leave division rank blank where a tie-breaker would be required.
suggestions.rationale: Publishing an inferred division order would be exactly the fabrication this project is built to avoid.
suggestions.evidence: The official tiebreaking procedure lists twelve ordered steps, none of which are in the standings snapshot held here.
suggestions.risk: Readers may expect a division column. Mitigation: a one-line explanation beside the table.

suggestions.title: Price nothing, and say so in the masthead
suggestions.problem: A research site that shows model output next to a sport invites the reader to assume a price is implied.
suggestions.proposal: Keep every price, hold, ROI and closing-line field blank and state the reason once, prominently, with the source-rights citation.
suggestions.rationale: The alternative is to display fair-odds numbers that look executable but are not, which is how research sites mislead people.
suggestions.evidence: NFL.com publishes no odds. The repository holds no licensed price feed. NFL terms do not grant redistribution or gambling-related rights.
suggestions.effort: Already implemented; needs to stay implemented.
suggestions.risk: The site looks emptier than competitors. That is the correct trade for a verification-first project.

suggestions.title: Make the anti-luck mechanism structural rather than editorial
suggestions.problem: Written promises about not rewarding luck do not survive contact with a leaderboard that someone wants to win.
suggestions.proposal: Build the scoring so a lucky entry cannot reach the top: rank on a lower confidence bound, require a frozen forward period, and require a declared trial count.
suggestions.rationale: A rule enforced by the build cannot be waived in a good week.
suggestions.evidence: Three scoring choices are already specified in the competition ledger; none is implemented because no entry is eligible.
suggestions.risk: With small samples the lower bound is very punishing and the board may stay empty for a long time. That is the intended behaviour.
suggestions.gate: Implements G07, G08 and G09 for the board.

suggestions.title: Correct the repository's stale self-description before adding more features
suggestions.problem: The root README and the committed static-check evidence describe a smaller site than the one that exists, so a reader cannot tell which numbers are current.
suggestions.proposal: Regenerate the evidence artefacts and rewrite the summary metrics from the build output rather than by hand, then have CI fail if they drift.
suggestions.rationale: A verification-first dashboard whose own description is out of date has already lost the argument.
suggestions.evidence: See the repository review page: README metrics, static-check counts and the snapshot-date stamp all disagree with the current build.
suggestions.risk: Touching shared files owned by other sessions. Mitigation: logged as a cross-scope request, not edited here.

suggestions.title: Show the data you do not have, next to the data you do
suggestions.problem: Every dashboard lists what it collected. Almost none lists what it decided not to collect, which is where the real limitations live.
suggestions.proposal: Add a coverage table per category: source available, source read, rows captured, rows excluded and why.
suggestions.rationale: It converts an invisible gap into a reviewable one and stops readers assuming full coverage.
suggestions.evidence: This repository captures 3 of 32 club depth charts, 1 week of injury reports, and 0 price observations.

suggestions.title: Add a second independent source for every official figure before calling it verified
suggestions.problem: A single page read once is a transcription, not a verification. Rounding artefacts in the passing table show that a single source can contain internal inconsistencies.
suggestions.proposal: For each figure that drives a conclusion, require a second, independent official source, or mark it 'single-source transcription'.
suggestions.rationale: It is the difference between 'we read the page' and 'we checked the number'.
suggestions.evidence: The passing-average discrepancy would have gone unnoticed without an internal recomputation.
suggestions.risk: Second sources for official NFL figures are scarce and often reproduce the same upstream feed, which would give false comfort. The badge must say which kind of check was done.
